deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page: no formulas, derivations or computations. It is part of a draft official report (Gutachten) from Göttingen to the Royal Hanoverian government, through the Curatorium/Curatorialreferent. The report answers a diplomatic ('gesandtschaftliche') note about Prussian participation in J. J. Baeyer's proposed Central European arc measurement (Mitteleuropäische Gradmessung, proposed 1861, organised from 1862). Riemann is named in the third person, so the text is probably a collective faculty or committee report in a clerk's or colleague's hand with corrections, not a Riemann autograph.

Content, in order:
(a) Top, as a quotation continued from the margin of the previous page: Gauss, 'Bestimmung des Breitenunterschiedes zwischen den Sternwarten von Göttingen und Altona' (1828), Art. 20. Gauss hopes that all European observatories will one day be linked trigonometrically, since chains already run from Scotland to the Adriatic and from Formentera to [Dunkirk?], though only partly published. He urges that unpublished materials be made known. The last two lines of the quotation are underlined.
(b) Main column, continuing point 2 from the previous page. The person entrusted with publishing the Hanoverian arc measurement (Gauss's triangulation of Hanover) should be instructed ('mit Anweisung zu versehen sein') to contact Professor Schering, so as to use the material in Gauss's handwritten Nachlass. If the work is instead done in Göttingen, all relevant files held in Hannover must be handed over.
(c) Point 3, on the higher scientific aim of exact knowledge of the figure of the Earth. Professor Riemann should be authorised, as the diplomatic note requests, to contact Generalleutnant z. D. Baeyer, the Prussian plenipotentiary, for deeper consultation. He is not to be obliged to direct such work or to take part in it under someone else's direction.
(d) Bottom, pencil draft, partly struck out and partly lost at the torn edge. Professor Riemann, to whom the matter was referred besides the Curatorial referee Hofrat [name uncertain], has declared [...] expert opinion [...].

The only 'problem served' is administrative and scientific-political: how Hannover/Göttingen should take part in the European geodetic survey, and what Riemann's role as a theoretical adviser on the figure of the Earth should be.
errors: No mathematical content, so no mathematical errors to check.
The quotation is a paraphrase or transcription of Gauss (1828, Art. 20). Exact agreement with Gauss's printed wording cannot be verified from the image alone.

results.what: Recommendation that Riemann be authorised to consult with J. J. Baeyer on the Central European arc measurement (figure of the Earth), without any obligation to direct or execute survey work.
results.modern_name: Administrative/historical document on Riemann's involvement in the Mitteleuropäische Gradmessung (c. 1862)

results.what: Quotation of Gauss's 1828 hope for a trigonometric connection of all European observatories, used to justify publishing the Hanoverian arc measurement using Gauss's Nachlass (via Schering).
results.modern_name: Gauss, Breitenunterschied Göttingen–Altona, Art. 20 (1828); publication of the Hannoversche Gradmessung

deep.surprise_reason: This is a purely administrative/scientific-policy document with no mathematics. Riemann's consultation on Baeyer's Gradmessung and Schering's role with Gauss's Nachlass are known biographical facts. The page adds archival detail, such as the explicit restriction on Riemann's obligations, but nothing mathematically new.
transcription_corrections: Main column, first line: 'verstehen [-sich-] {+sein+}' should read 'versehen [-sich-] {+sein+}'. It continues the previous page's 'so dürfte sie mit Anweisung zu versehen sein, sich mit dem Professor Schering ... in Verbindung zu setzen'. The struck word is 'sich' and 'sein' is written above it.

Quotation line 4: 'Dünen[?]' is very uncertain. Given the Delambre–Méchain/Biot–Arago meridian chain, the intended place is probably Dünkirchen (Dunkirk); possibly Dunnose. Check against Gauss's printed text.
The marginal number '73' is the folio number, not part of the text.
The bottom pencil lines are fragmentary and partly lost at the tear. Readings 'Curatorialrefe[rent]' and 'Hofrat Radicke[?]' are uncertain.
